overview: This bill, also called the RAM Act, would require the Small Business Administration (SBA), through its Office of Manufacturing and Trade, to set up a webpage within 60 days to help small businesses move some or all of their manufacturing back to the United States, a process often called onshoring or reshoring. The page would list SBA and partner contacts and include a free tool to help businesses find organizations that can assist with the move. The SBA would gather suggestions each year for improving the page, study how well it works, and report to Congress. All of the bill's requirements would end after four years. As of October 9, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say small manufacturers thinking about bringing production home often don't know where to start, and a single government webpage pointing them to help is a low-cost way to support U.S. manufacturing.
against: Critics say a webpage is a modest step that does little to address the costs that drive manufacturing overseas, and that similar information is already available from other government programs.
